title: Polish Confession: not justified forensically by inherent justice
source_text: XLIII. Ne quis autem adversariorum calumniari possit, hanc non esse germanam Reformatorum sententiam, dum negant nos formaliter coram Deo justificari per justi-tiam quae nobis inhaeret, illosque plus detrahere justitiae inhaerenti quam tribuamus, hic inserere visum est, quae paucis hac de re tradit jam citata Confessio Reformatorum ex Polonia, cap. 4. sect. 2. num. 13. Negamus etiam, inquit, per justitiam illam inhaerentem propriam nos ita justificari, ut per, & propter eam coram judicio Dei a reatu mortis absolvamur, in filios adoptemur, & vita aeterna digni pronunciemur, quo sensu forensi vox justificandi a Spiritu Sancto in hac doctrina usurpatur. Etsi enim lato sensu dici possit, nos per charitatem, aliasque virtutes infusas justificari, id est, justos, sanctosque fieri, haec tamen justitia in hac vita imperfecta est, eaque, ut supra dictum, coram severo Dei judicio nequaquam potest consistere; quod solum in hac doctrina maxime spectatur.
pass_a_gloss: But lest any of the adversaries be able to calumniate that this is not the genuine mind of the Reformers when they deny that we are formally justified before God by the righteousness that inheres in us, and that they detract more from inherent righteousness than we ascribe, it has seemed good to insert here what the Confession of the Reformers from Poland already cited briefly hands down on this matter (chapter 4, section 2, number 13): We also deny, it says, that by that inherent righteousness of our own we are so justified that by and because of it we are absolved before God's judgment from the guilt of death, adopted as sons, and pronounced worthy of eternal life—in which forensic sense the word justify is used by the Holy Spirit in this doctrine. For although in a broad sense it can be said that we are justified by charity and the other infused virtues—that is, made just and holy—yet this righteousness in this life is imperfect, and, as said above, can by no means stand before God's severe judgment; which alone is chiefly looked to in this doctrine.
pass_b_english: Polish Confession: we deny being forensically justified by inherent justice so as to be cleared of death's guilt and declared heirs of life for it.
Broadly one may say infused virtues make us just/holy, yet that justice cannot stand the severe tribunal.
